headline: Apple's market value closed above $5 trillion for the first time on Wednesday, making it only the second company after Nvidia to reach that level.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; it is a price milestone with a side link to AI.
importance_line: Apple shareholders, including pension funds, gain from the milestone and the new chief executive John Ternus now faces pressure to keep growth going; the doubt is that a share price level says little about AI progress, where Apple has lagged some rivals.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, as relayed by Yahoo Finance, that Apple shares rose 0.5% to a record $342.96 on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, valuing the company at about $5.005 trillion as investors weigh the first weeks under chief executive John Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook on 1 Sep. The Journal notes that Apple has lagged some rivals in building advanced AI models and has turned to partners, including Google, to improve Siri.
notes: Read at Yahoo Finance, which relays the Wall Street Journal; the Journal's own page was not opened. Source credited to the Journal per the chain rule. AI relevance is secondary (AI lag, competition from OpenAI); the main event is a market-value milestone.
